input.sha256_scope: The committed classic-v1-e2e-reading-order/input.png, which two of the six cases use directly and in 180-degree rotation. The other four cases are deterministic synthetic crops generated by formula on both sides and carry no separate payload.
input.provenance: No new input pixels. Two cases reuse an already-committed and already-reviewed fixture PNG; the other four are generated by a trivial closed-form expression reproduced identically in the capture tool and the Rust test.

limitations: The preprocessing sequence is transcribed from the artifact's inference.yml rather than imported, because for this capability the contract lives in the artifact and there is no Python predictor for the pinned model. An upstream change to that config would not be detected here.

The model outputs are recorded, not reproduced offline: the committed fixture checks that this port builds the same input tensor and reaches the same verdict from the recorded output. Running the real model needs the provisioned artifact and the ignored gate.

Six cases with one real image. Four are synthetic and exercise arithmetic rather than text; only the reading-order pair exercises what the classifier is actually for, and both members of that pair are the same image.
The artifacts declared for this fixture are null because none is committed. The model digest is recorded inside expected.json for traceability, not as a provisioned dependency.
